title: Does Policy Mirror Descent Converge in Policy with Non-Decomposable Mirror Maps? A Counterexample

paper.title: Does Policy Mirror Descent Converge in Policy with Non-Decomposable Mirror Maps? A Counterexample
paper.abstract: Abstract Policy mirror descent (PMD) refers to a class of policy optimization methods associated with different mirror maps. For a broad class of decomposable Legendre mirror maps encompassing many standard choices, Li and Wei (2026) show that the PMD policy sequence converges to an optimal policy from any admissible initialization under any positive constant step size, even when the optimal policy is not unique. In this note, we provide a counterexample with assistance from OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 model, showing that PMD with a non-decomposable Legendre mirror map need not converge in policy.

sections.heading: 1 Introduction
sections.text: Let Δ ⁡ ( 𝒳 ) \Delta(\mathcal{X}) denote the probabilistic simplex over some finite set 𝒳 \mathcal{X} . A finite discounted Markov decision process (MDP) is specified by a tuple ( 𝒮 , 𝒜 , P , r , γ , μ ) (\mathcal{S},\mathcal{A},P,r,\gamma,\mu) , where 𝒮 \mathcal{S} and 𝒜 \mathcal{A} are finite state and action spaces, respectively, P : 𝒮 × 𝒜 → Δ ⁡ ( 𝒮 ) P:\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{A}\to\Delta(\mathcal{S}) is the transition kernel, r : 𝒮 × 𝒜 → [ 0 , 1 ] r:\mathcal{S}\times\mathcal{A}\to[0,1] is the reward function, γ ∈ [ 0 , 1 ) \gamma\in[0,1) is the discount factor, and μ ∈ Δ ⁡ ( 𝒮 ) \mu\in\Delta(\mathcal{S}) is the initial state distribution. Given a policy π : 𝒮 → Δ ⁡ ( 𝒜 ) \pi:\mathcal{S}\to\Delta(\mathcal{A}) , a trajectory { ( s t , a t , r t ) } t ≥ 0 \{(s_{t},a_{t},r_{t})\}_{t\geq 0} is generated as follows: the initial state is sampled from s 0 ∼ μ s_{0}\sim\mu , and at each time step t ≥ 0 t\geq 0 , the agent selects an action a t ∼ π ( ⋅ ∣ s t ) a_{t}\sim\pi(\cdot\mid s_{t}) , receives the reward r t = r ⁡ ( s t , a t ) r_{t}=r(s_{t},a_{t}) , and transitions to the next state s t + 1 ∼ P ( ⋅ ∣ s t , a t ) s_{t+1}\sim P(\cdot\mid s_{t},a_{t}) . The state value and the action value functions are defined as ∀ s ∈ 𝒮 , a ∈ 𝒜 : \displaystyle\forall\,s\in\mathcal{S},\;a\in\mathcal{A}:\quad V π ( s ) := 𝔼 [ ∑ t = 0 ∞ γ t r ( s t , a t ) | s 0 = s , π ] , \displaystyle V^{\pi}(s):=\mathbb{E}\,\Bigg[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}r(s_{t},a_{t})\;\Big|\;s_{0}=s,\,\pi\Bigg], Q π ( s , a ) := 𝔼 [ ∑ t = 0 ∞ γ t r ( s t , a t ) | ( s 0 , a 0 ) = ( s , a ) , π ] . \displaystyle Q^{\pi}(s,a):=\mathbb{E}\,\Bigg[\sum_{t=0}^{\infty}\gamma^{t}r(s_{t},a_{t})\;\Big|\;(s_{0},a_{0})=(s,a),\,\pi\Bigg]. Policy mirror descent (PMD) updates policies using a Bregman divergence induced by a convex mirror map h : ℝ | 𝒜 | → ℝ ∪ { + ∞ } h:\mathbb{R}^{|\mathcal{A}|}\to\mathbb{R}\cup\{+\infty\} . Assume that Δ ⁡ ( 𝒜 ) ⊆ dom ⁡ h \Delta(\mathcal{A})\subseteq\operatorname{dom}h and that h h is differentiable on int ⁡ ( dom ⁡ h ) \operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}h) . Given a current policy π \pi satisfying π ( ⋅ ∣ s ) ∈ int ( dom h ) \pi(\cdot\mid s)\in\operatorname{int}(\operatorname{dom}h) for all s ∈ 𝒮 s\in\mathcal{S} , PMD computes a new policy based on the action value function Q π Q^{\pi} by solving the following optimization problem at each state: (PMD) ∀ s ∈ 𝒮 : π + ( ⋅ | s ) ∈ arg ⁡ max p ∈ Δ ⁡ ( 𝒜 ) { η ⟨ p , Q π ( s , ⋅ ) ⟩ − D h ( p ∥ π ( ⋅ | s ) ) } , \displaystyle\mbox{(PMD)}\quad\forall\,s\in\mathcal{S}:\;\;\pi^{+}(\cdot|s)\in\underset{p\in\Delta(\mathcal{A})}{\arg\max}\;\Big\{\eta\,\big\langle p,\;Q^{\pi}(s,\cdot)\big\rangle-D_{h}(p\,\|\,\pi(\cdot|s))\Big\}, (1) where η > 0 \eta>0 is the update step size and D h ( p ∥ q ) := h ( p ) − h ( q ) − ⟨ ∇ h ( q ) , p − q ⟩ ) D_{h}(p\,\|\,q):=h(p)-h(q)-\left\langle\nabla h(q),\;p-q\right\rangle) is the Bregman divergence. Different choices of the mirror map h h yield different policy optimization methods. In particular, when h h is the squared function h ⁡ ( p ) = 1 2 ​ ‖ p ‖ 2 2 h(p)=\frac{1}{2}\|p\|_{2}^{2} or the negative Shannon entropy h ⁡ ( p ) = ∑ a ∈ 𝒜 p ⁡ ( a ) ​ log ⁡ p ⁡ ( a ) h(p)=\sum_{a\in\mathcal{A}}p(a)\log p(a) , PMD deduces to projected Q-ascent (PQA, Xiao (2022) ; Liu et al. (2025a) ) and softmax natural policy gradient (softmax NPG, Xiao (2022) ; Agarwal et al. (2021) ), respectively. The global convergence in value of PMD has been extensively studied. When h h is of Legendre type, it is shown in Xiao (2022) ; Lan (2021) that the state value function of PMD V π k V^{\pi_{k}} converges to the optimal value V ∗ V^{*} in a dimension-free O ⁡ ( 1 / k ) O(1/k) sublinear rate under arbitrary constant step size η > 0 \eta>0 . For adaptive or geometrically increasing step sizes, the global linear convergence can be established ( Xiao, 2022 ; Johnson et al., 2023 ; Alfano et al., 2023 ) . Several variants of PMD have also been investigated, including regularized PMD ( Lan, 2021 ; Cen et al., 2022 ; Zhan et al., 2023 ) , homotopic PMD ( Li et al., 2023 ) , TD-PMD ( Liu et al., 2025b ; Li et al., 2025 ; Geist et al., 2019 ) . Beyond value convergence, policy convergence of PMD has also been studied. For decomposable mirror maps of the form h ⁡ ( p ) = ∑ a ∈ 𝒜 ψ ⁡ ( p ⁡ ( a ) ) h(p)=\sum_{a\in\mathcal{A}}\psi(p(a)) , where ψ \psi satisfies standard Legendre-type assumptions, Li and Wei (2026) establish that the policy sequence generated by PMD converges to a limiting optimal policy under any constant step size η > 0 \eta>0 , even when the optimal policy is not unique. For mirror maps that need not be decomposable, Lin and Zhang (2022) establish finite-time convergence to an optimal policy under any constant step size, provided that h h is continuously differentiable on the entire probability simplex Δ ⁡ ( 𝒜 ) \Delta(\mathcal{A}) and satisfies an L L -cocoercivity condition. These results raise the following question: Does PMD converge in policy for every non-decomposable Legendre mirror map? This note, however, gives a negative answer by providing a counter example. The counterexample is based on a non-decomposable mirror map h h that combines algebraic, logarithmic, and trigonometric terms and satisfies the Legendre conditions: it is proper, closed, convex, essentially strictly convex, and essentially smooth. The associated MDP is a three-armed bandit with 𝒮 = { s } \mathcal{S}=\{s\} and 𝒜 = { a 1 , a 2 , a 3 } \mathcal{A}=\{a_{1},a_{2},a_{3}\} , where a 1 a_{1} and a 2 a_{2} are optimal actions and a 3 a_{3} is suboptimal. By computation, it is shown that the policy sequence generated by PMD from a particular initialization on this example oscillates infinitely times due to the periodicity of trigonometric component in h h .

sections.heading: 4 Conclusion
sections.text: This note constructs a Legendre but non-decomposable mirror map and a three-armed bandit problem for which PMD fails to converge in the policy domain under any positive constant step size and a suitable initialization. Although the value sequence converges to the optimal value, the policy sequence has a nontrivial continuum of optimal accumulation points and therefore does not converge in the policy domain. This counterexample shows that the Legendre conditions alone are insufficient to guarantee policy convergence of PMD, and that additional structural conditions, such as decomposability, are needed for a general policy convergence guarantee.

October 14, 2026 Abstract Policy mirror descent (PMD) refers to a class of policy optimization methods associated with different mirror maps. For a broad class of decomposable Legendre mirror maps encompassing many standard choices, Li and Wei (2026) show that the PMD policy sequence converges to an optimal policy from any admissible initialization under any positive constant step size, even when the optimal policy is not unique. In this note, we provide a counterexample with assistance from OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 model, showing that PMD with a non-decomposable Legendre mirror map need not converge in policy. 1 Introduction Let Δ ⁡ ( 𝒳 ) \Delta(\mathcal{X}) denote the probabilistic simplex over some finite set 𝒳 \mathcal{X} . When h h is of Legendre type, it is shown in Xiao (2022) ; Lan (2021) that the state value function of PMD V π k V^{\pi_{k}} converges to the optimal value V ∗ V^{*} in a dimension-free O ⁡ ( 1 / k ) O(1/k) sublinear rate under arbitrary constant step size η > 0 \eta>0 . Several variants of PMD have also been investigated, including regularized PMD ( Lan, 2021 ; Cen et al., 2022 ; Zhan et al., 2023 ) , homotopic PMD ( Li et al., 2023 ) , TD-PMD ( Liu et al., 2025b ; Li et al., 2025 ; Geist et al., 2019 ) .
